title: Read the annual-energy number
hook: The labels say €60 and €105 a year. Over 8 years, the difference between two fridges is?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Translate a stated annual energy figure into a multiyear running-cost model.

misconception: An annual energy label is already the multiyear cost.
objective: Translate a stated annual energy figure into a multiyear running-cost model.

claims.text: Illustrative annual quantities are 200kWh and 350kWh. Both are priced at €0.30/kWh every year. Scaled model; Illustrative annual use of 200 or 350 kWh at €0.30/kWh, unchanged across years.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by this lesson's declared expressions; each card prints its working in plain words. At Years=8, A=€480.00 and B=€840.00. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",200,"x",0.3]; B=["*",350,"x",0.3]; x denotes Years. At x=2, A=120, B=210. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md. Reset to unverified by demo-builder 2026-10-15 (v2, company/decisions/2026-10-15-lifehacks-r11-fix-plan.md): v2 stage: plain-words readouts (TP-7a), no 'Full scale' label (TP-7b), money to 2 decimals (TP-7c); A=["*", 200, "x", 0.3], B=["*", 350, "x", 0.3], variable {"label": "Years", "start": 8, "min": 1, "max": 10, "unit": "", "step": 1}. 200kWh × €0.30 = €60/year; 350kWh × €0.30 = €105/year; gap €45/year; over 8 years A = €480, B = €840, difference 8 × €45 = €360. Bracket fill: [a] = the two labels' yearly costs €60 and €105 (the line's 'The label says €[a]' is written as 'The labels say €60 and €105'). | FC pass 51 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15, W-1101): VERIFIED. Own run: at 8 years A = 200 × 8 × 0.3 = €480.00, B = 350 × 8 × 0.3 = €840.00; readouts '200 kWh × 8 years × €0.30' etc. Energy picture: line samples at 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 years on a fixed scale (top label €1,050.00, the range maximum). Note for demo-builder: at 1 year the readout reads '1 years'. Record: company/reviews/lh-annual-label-cost/2026-10-14-fact-check.md, Pass 51.

claims.text: Multiply annual energy by years and the stated unit price. The two labels differ by €45 a year (150kWh × €0.30), so the gap grows every year: €360 over 8 years. This assumes unchanged use and tariff; it is not a measured forecast for a named product.

At x=2, A=120, B=210. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. claims.text: For a stated constant load, kWh = watts × hours ÷ 1000. Running cost = kWh × the stated price per kWh; stated fixed costs are added separately.
